verses.1:1: The word of the LORD which came to Joel son of Pethuel.
verses.1:2: Listen to this, elders, and give ear, all inhabitants of the land. Has this happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
verses.1:3: Recount it to your children, and let your children recount it to their children, and their children to a following generation.
verses.1:4: What remained from the shearing locust, the swarming locust ate; and what remained from the swarming locust, the crawling locust ate; and what remained from the crawling locust, the consuming locust ate.
verses.1:5: Wake up, drunkards, and weep, and wail, all drinkers of wine, over the sweet wine, for it has been cut off from your mouths.
verses.1:6: For a nation has come up against My land, mighty and innumerable; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and the fangs of a lioness belong to it.
verses.1:7: It has turned My vine into a desolation and My fig tree into splinters; it has stripped it completely bare and thrown it down; its branches have turned white.
verses.1:8: Lament like a virgin wrapped in sackcloth over the husband of her youth.
verses.1:9: Grain offering and drink offering have been cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests, the LORD's ministers, are in mourning.
verses.1:10: The field is devastated, the ground mourns; for the grain is devastated, the new wine has dried up, the fresh oil languishes.
verses.1:11: Be ashamed, farmers; wail, vineyard keepers, over the wheat and over the barley, for the harvest of the field has perished.
verses.1:12: The vine has dried up, and the fig tree languishes; the pomegranate, the palm also, and the apple tree—all the trees of the field have dried up; indeed, joy has dried up away from the sons of mankind.
verses.1:13: Put on sackcloth and mourn, priests; wail, ministers of the altar! Come, spend the night in sackcloth, ministers of my God, because grain offering and drink offering have been withheld from the house of your God.
verses.1:14: Sanctify a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly. Gather the elders, all inhabitants of the land, to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
verses.1:15: Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is near, and it comes like devastation from the Almighty.
verses.1:16: Has not food been cut off before our eyes, and from the house of our God, gladness and rejoicing?
verses.1:17: The seed grains have shriveled beneath their clods; the storehouses stand desolate, the granaries have been torn down, for the grain has dried up.
verses.1:18: How the animals groan! The herds of cattle are bewildered because there is no pasture for them; even the flocks of sheep suffer punishment.
verses.1:19: To You, LORD, I call out, because fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and a flame has scorched all the trees of the field.
verses.1:20: Even the animals of the field long for You, because the channels of water have dried up, and fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
verses.2:1: Blow a ram's horn in Zion, and raise an alarm on My holy mountain! Let all inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of the LORD is coming, for it is near.
verses.2:2: A day of darkness and deep gloom, a day of cloud and heavy darkness! Like dawn spread out over the mountains—a vast and mighty people; its like has never occurred from ages past, nor will it happen again after it through the years of generation after generation.
verses.2:3: Before it fire devours, and behind it a flame scorches. The land is like the garden of Eden before it, yet behind it a wilderness of desolation; and truly there is no escape from it.
verses.2:4: Its appearance is like the appearance of horses, and like horsemen, so they run.
verses.2:5: Like the sound of chariots they bound upon the tops of the mountains, like the sound of a flame of fire devouring stubble, like a mighty people arrayed for battle.
verses.2:6: Before it peoples writhe in anguish; all faces lose their color.
verses.2:7: Like mighty warriors they run; like men of war they climb a wall. Each one marches in his own ways, and they do not veer from their paths.
verses.2:8: Not one crowds another; each marches on his own course. Even when they plunge through the weapons, they do not break off.
verses.2:9: They rush through the city, they run along the wall, they climb up the houses; through the windows they enter like a thief.
verses.2:10: Before it the earth trembles, the heavens shake; sun and moon grow dark, and stars withdraw their radiance.
verses.2:11: And the LORD gives forth His voice before His army, for His camp is very vast, for mighty is the one who executes His word. For great is the day of the LORD and exceedingly awesome; and who can bear it?
verses.2:12: "And even now," declares the LORD, "turn back to Me with your whole heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning."
verses.2:13: Tear your heart and not your garments, and turn back to the LORD your God, for He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in loyal love, and relenting over calamity.
verses.2:14: Who knows? He may turn back and relent, and leave a blessing behind Him—grain offering and drink offering for the LORD your God.
verses.2:15: Blow a ram's horn in Zion; sanctify a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly.
verses.2:16: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders; gather the little ones and those nursing at the breast. Let the bridegroom go out from his chamber and the bride from her bridal canopy.
verses.2:17: Between the portico and the altar let the priests, the LORD's ministers, weep, and let them say, "Spare Your people, LORD, and do not give Your heritage over to reproach, for nations to rule over them. Why should they say among the peoples, 'Where is their God?'"
verses.2:18: Then the LORD grew zealous for His land and took pity on His people.
verses.2:19: And the LORD answered and said to His people, "Look, I am sending you the grain, the new wine, and the fresh oil, and you will be satisfied with it; and I will no longer make you a reproach among the nations.
verses.2:20: And the northern one I will remove far from you, and I will banish it into a dry and desolate land—its front into the eastern sea and its rear into the western sea; and its stench will rise, and its foul odor will go up, for it has done great things.
verses.2:21: Do not be afraid, ground; rejoice and be glad, for the LORD has done great things.
verses.2:22: Do not be afraid, animals of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness have sprouted green; for the tree has borne its fruit; fig tree and vine have yielded their strength.
verses.2:23: And children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the LORD your God, for He has given you the early rain in righteousness, and He has sent down for you rain—early rain and late rain—at the first.
verses.2:24: And the threshing floors will be filled with grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and fresh oil.
verses.2:25: And I will repay you for the years that the swarming locust has eaten—the crawling locust, the consuming locust, and the shearing locust—My great army that I sent among you.
verses.2:26: And you will eat abundantly and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has acted wondrously with you; and My people will never be ashamed.
verses.2:27: And you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God and there is no one else; and My people will never be ashamed."
verses.3:1: And afterward it will happen that I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.
verses.3:2: And even on the male servants and on the female servants, in those days I will pour out My Spirit.
verses.3:3: And I will display portents in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.
verses.3:4: The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the coming of the day of the LORD, great and awesome.
verses.3:5: And it will happen that everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be rescued; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, just as the LORD has said, and among the survivors whom the LORD calls.
verses.4:1: For look, during those days and at that time, when I bring back the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,
verses.4:2: I will assemble all the nations and bring them down into the Valley of Jehoshaphat, and I will contend in judgment with them there on account of My people and My heritage Israel, whom they dispersed among the nations; and they apportioned My land.
verses.4:3: And over My people they cast lots; they gave a boy for a prostitute, and they sold a girl for wine and drank.
verses.4:4: And furthermore, what are you to Me, Tyre and Sidon, and all the districts of Philistia? Is it retaliation that you are paying back to Me? And if you are retaliating against Me, quickly, speedily I will bring back your retaliation upon your head.
verses.4:5: For you took My silver and My gold, and you brought My choice treasures into your temples,
verses.4:6: and you sold the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem to the Greeks, so as to put them far away from their border.
verses.4:7: Look, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will bring back your retaliation upon your head.
verses.4:8: And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, to a far-off nation, for the LORD has spoken.
verses.4:9: Announce this among the nations: Consecrate war! Rouse the warriors! Let all the men of war approach; let them come up!
verses.4:10: Hammer your plowshares into swords, and your pruning knives into lances; let the weak one say, "I am a warrior."
verses.4:11: Hurry and come, all you nations from all around, and assemble together! Bring down Your warriors there, LORD!
verses.4:12: Let the nations be roused and come up into the Valley of Jehoshaphat; for I will sit there to judge all the nations from all around.
verses.4:13: Thrust in the sickle, for the harvest has ripened! Come, tread, for the winepress is filled; the vats are overflowing, for abundant is their wickedness.
verses.4:14: Throngs, throngs in the Valley of Decision! For near is the day of the LORD in the Valley of Decision.
verses.4:15: Sun and moon darken, and stars withdraw their radiance.
verses.4:16: And from Zion the LORD roars, and from Jerusalem He raises His voice, and heaven and earth quake; yet the LORD is a shelter for His people and a fortress for the children of Israel.
verses.4:17: And you will know that I, the LORD your God, am dwelling in Zion, My holy mountain; and Jerusalem will be holy, and foreigners will not pass through her again.
verses.4:18: And it will be on that day that the mountains will drip fresh wine, and the hills will run with milk, and all the channels of Judah will run with water; and a spring will come out from the house of the LORD and water the Wadi of Shittim.
verses.4:19: Egypt will become a desolation, and Edom will become a wilderness of desolation, on account of the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.
verses.4:20: Yet Judah will remain inhabited forever, and Jerusalem for generation after generation.
verses.4:21: And I will clear their blood that I have not cleared, and the LORD dwells in Zion.

notes.1:4: The four Hebrew terms gazam, arbeh, yeleq, and chasil (repeated in a different order in 2:25) denote either distinct varieties or successive developmental stages of locusts; their exact zoological distinctions remain uncertain.
notes.1:6: "My land" (together with "My vine" and "My fig tree" in v. 7) reflects the LORD claiming Judah as His covenant possession (cf. 2:1, 18), though some understand the first-person pronouns as the prophet speaking on behalf of the community.
notes.1:11: Hebrew plays on near-identical Hiphil forms of yavesh ("dry up," vv. 10, 12, 17) and bosh ("be ashamed" or "fail," here as a Hiphil imperative and again in v. 12 with "joy").
notes.1:15: Hebrew creates a striking sound play in ke-shod mi-shaddai ("like devastation from the Almighty"), echoing the Pual verb shuddad ("is devastated") in v. 10.
notes.1:17: Several terms in this verse occur only here in the Hebrew Bible: aveshu ("have shriveled"), ferudot ("seed grains"), megrefotehem ("their clods," or possibly "their shovels"), and mammegurot ("granaries," cognate with megurah in Hag 2:19).
notes.2:2: Following the Masoretic vocalization, ke-shachar means "like dawn," picturing the swarm sweeping swiftly across the mountain ridges; some modern versions emend the vowels to ke-shechor ("like blackness").
notes.2:6: The rare idiom qibbetsu fa'rur (also in Nah 2:10, MT 2:11) is understood either as "withdraw their flush/glow" (losing color, from a root meaning "glow/beauty") or as "gather blackness" (from a noun for a soot-blackened cooking pot).
notes.2:17: The phrase li-meshol-bam goyim uses the idiom mashal be- ("rule over"), yielding "for nations to rule over them"; an alternative reading derives the verb from a homonymous root meaning "make a byword/taunt of."
notes.2:18: The Masoretic Text shifts here to wayyiqtol narrative past verbs ("grew zealous... took pity... answered... said" in vv. 18-19), presenting the LORD's merciful intervention as an accomplished turning point rather than a conditional future.
notes.2:23: The noun ha-moreh means "the early rain" (matching moreh u-malqosh later in the verse), though some ancient traditions read it as "the teacher" ("teacher of righteousness"); li-tsedaqah ("in righteousness") may convey "in right measure" or "for vindication," and ba-ri'shon ("at the first") can also mean "in the first month" (whereas the Septuagint reads "as before").
notes.3:1: Hebrew Masoretic numbering begins chapter 3 here (corresponding to 2:28-32 in most English Bibles); unlike the quotation in Acts 2:17, the Hebrew text reads simply achare-khen ("afterward") and et-ruchi ("My Spirit").
notes.3:5: The noun peletah ("deliverance," or concretely "those who escape") echoes 2:3 ("no escape"), and the final prepositional phrase u-vas-seridim ("and among the survivors") parallels "on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem" as the sphere where deliverance is found.
notes.4:1: The written ketiv reads the Qal imperfect form (אשוב, "I return"), while the read qere (translated here) has the Hiphil imperfect (אָשִׁיב, "I bring back/restore"). The idiom "bring back the fortunes" (lit. "bring back the turning/captivity") denotes a full reversal of Judah and Jerusalem's distressed state.
notes.4:2: The name Jehoshaphat means "the LORD judges," creating a wordplay with the following Niphal verb "I will contend in judgment" (וְנִשְׁפַּטְתִּי, from שׁפט), echoed again in 4:12.
notes.4:11: The imperative "Hurry" translates the hapax legomenon עוּשׁוּ, understood in Hebrew tradition as "hasten" (or alternatively "assemble/come to aid"). Following the Masoretic atnah accent after "assemble together," "there" (שָׁמָּה) is taken with the Hiphil imperative הַנְחַת ("bring down") in the appeal to the LORD.
notes.4:13: The imperative "tread" (רְדוּ) is taken from רדה ("tread" grapes in the winepress), though the form can equally be parsed as the Qal imperative of ירד ("go down" into the winepress).
notes.4:21: The Masoretic Text repeats the Piel of נקה ("clear, acquit, leave unpunished")—weqatal "I will clear" followed by negated qatal "I have not cleared"—indicating either the final pardon of Judah's bloodguilt or an unmarked rhetorical question ("Will I leave their blood unpunished? I have not"). Ancient versions such as the Septuagint instead read "avenge" (reflecting the root נקם).
